# AbstractFramework
> Meta-package + documentation hub for the AbstractFramework ecosystem (durable, observable agents/workflows).

This repo pins ecosystem package versions and provides a tiny helper API in `abstractframework/`.
Most runtime behavior lives in the individual package repos (AbstractCore/Runtime/Agent/Flow/Gateway/Code).
AbstractCode is a Rust terminal client (`cargo install abstractcode`) plus a browser client (served by the gateway at `/apps/code/`, or `npx @abstractframework/code --gateway-url <url>`); both need a running gateway and both manage automations.

Quick commands:
- Mac installer: download `https://github.com/lpalbou/AbstractFramework/releases/latest/download/AbstractFramework-Installer.pkg` and double-click it; the package is not signed with an Apple Developer ID, so the first time allow it with Open Anyway in System Settings > Privacy & Security; it runs `install.sh --interactive` in Terminal. Remove with `Uninstall AbstractFramework.command` or `curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lpalbou/AbstractFramework/main/scripts/uninstall.sh | sh`
- One-line install (gateway + console, no admin, no system Python): `curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lpalbou/AbstractFramework/main/scripts/install.sh | sh` (Windows: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lpalbou/AbstractFramework/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex"`); installs uv + Python 3.12 + the pinned gateway (with local voice) as a uv tool, asks whether to start at login whenever a terminal exists (Enter = yes; no terminal or no answer within `--ask-wait` = off on a first install, kept on a re-run; the summary says how to turn it on), starts it on 127.0.0.1:8080, writes the local gateway pointer `~/.abstractframework/gateway.json` for this install (address only; `serve` keeps it current under its ownership rule) and opens `/console` through a one-time claim link; browser apps open through the gateway at `/apps/<app>/`; `--print` dry run, `--uninstall` to remove
- Upgrade: run the same install line again (the latest AbstractFramework release; profile, port, start at login, data and apps kept; Mac package: install the latest .pkg again); add `sh -s -- --pin latest` (Windows `-Pin latest`) for the newest gateway on PyPI; `uv tool upgrade abstractgateway` does not upgrade an installer install (it keeps the exact pinned version); apps: console Apps page or `abstractgateway apps update <app>`; right after a release, when a PyPI mirror does not list or serve a pinned version yet, the installer retries the same full install (15/30/60/120 s waits, 8 attempts, about 10 minutes) and never installs less; see docs/install.md#upgrade
- Network exposure: the gateway listens on this computer only (`localhost`) until you run `abstractgateway network set lan|internet` (or use the console / menu-bar icon); `service install` takes `--port`, and the login item runs plain `serve` so the Network setting applies
- Start either entry point and open the printed one-time link: `abstractcore serve` (http://127.0.0.1:8000/console#claim=…) or `abstractgateway serve` (http://127.0.0.1:8080/console#claim=…); both consoles have Models (catalog + fit verdict, download, delete) and Engines (detect, install) tabs, mirrored by `abstractcore models|engines` and `abstractgateway models|engines`
- Install pinned stack: `pip install abstractframework`
- Check install health: `abstractframework doctor`
- Print installer manifest: `abstractframework manifest`
- Show detected component versions: `python -c "from abstractframework import print_status; print_status()"`

Notes for LLMs working in this repo:
- Prefer `docs/` as the ecosystem-level source of truth.
- Keep changes minimal and ecosystem-level (docs + version pins).
- If you need to change runtime behavior, you likely want the relevant package repo instead of this meta repo.
- Gateway-first hosted browser setups use Gateway user auth, opaque browser
  sessions, and `/console` for account/admin/defaults management. AbstractFlow,
  AbstractCode Web, and AbstractObserver exchange user tokens for app-scoped
  browser sessions and do not persist bearer tokens in browser settings.
  Gateway login responses do not expose session ids/CSRF tokens in JSON, and
  default resolution is Core defaults -> Gateway baseline Core config ->
  per-runtime Core config override.
  Do not treat the bootstrap `ABSTRACTGATEWAY_AUTH_TOKEN` as a browser-user
  login token. Gateway session cookies are HTTP-only for the session id, use a
  separate CSRF cookie, set `Secure` only under HTTPS, expire, logout cleanly,
  and are revoked when the backing user is disabled/deleted/token-rotated.
- Gateway user isolation is enforced through per-principal runtime routing plus
  a central route-family policy. Ordinary users can use their own runs, ledgers,
  artifacts, KG/session memory, private workflows, session artifacts,
  prompt-cache session names, and runtime-scoped Core defaults. Admin-only workspace
  helpers/import/export and provider prompt-cache controls are advertised as
  unavailable in discovery with machine-readable `admin_required` metadata.
  Deleting a user reserves the retained runtime id for that principal so the
  runtime cannot be reassigned to a different same-tenant user while data is
  still retained. Admins may explicitly transfer a retained runtime to an
  existing same-tenant user or purge the retained runtime directory before
  releasing the runtime id for reuse.
- Gateway provider connections are Gateway-owned reusable profiles for OpenAI,
  Anthropic, OpenRouter, Portkey, LM Studio, Ollama, and custom
  OpenAI-compatible endpoints. They include a description, provider family,
  base URL, optional model allowlist, and a write-only API key. Discovery
  exposes them as virtual providers such as `endpoint:office-vllm`; Runtime
  resolves the virtual id into transient provider/base URL/key parameters
  without storing secrets in workflow JSON or browser storage.
- AbstractCore also supports local single-principal provider endpoint profiles
  through `abstractcore config set-provider ...`. These profiles expose the
  same virtual provider shape (`endpoint:<id>`) for Core-only developers, while
  Gateway remains responsible for hosted user/runtime scoping.
- Gateway Console separates provider configuration from defaults: the Providers
  tab stores endpoint URLs/API keys and tests discovery; the Defaults tab only
  maps capability routes to configured virtual providers and discovered models.
  LLM/embedding model pickers use Core `capability_route` filters such as
  `input.image,output.text` and `embedding.text`; generated-media defaults use
  capability plugin catalogs.
- AbstractFlow uses the same route-aware discovery for text model selectors and
  Models Catalog nodes. Gateway `/runs/start` accepts optional `thinking`, and
  Flow LLM Call/Agent nodes can set or pin `thinking` so reasoning controls
  flow through Runtime and AbstractAgent into Core.
- Hosted Flow, Code Web, and Observer use the server-configured Gateway URL on
  non-loopback UI hostnames. Browser-supplied Gateway URL changes are rejected
  unless the app-specific remote override is enabled behind access control.
  Host checks trust `Host` by default; forwarded host headers require an
  explicit trust-proxy env setting.
- Gateway workflow sharing uses the explicit workflow catalog, not another
  user's private `/bundles` directory. Catalog bundle versions are immutable,
  admins move default pointers and ACLs, and users start catalog workflows with
  `registry_scope: "tenant_catalog"` so the run executes in their own runtime.
  Catalog scope is explicit, direct private-bundle routes reject
  catalog-internal ids, and Gateway signs catalog workflow policy before
  passing it to Runtime.
- A packaged Gateway serves shipped workflow bundles out of the box, with no
  manual install: `basic-agent` (default chat agent), `coding-agent` (a
  verify-gated coder, `coder` entrypoint), `deep-research`, `co-scientist`,
  `docs-qa`, `abstractassistant-orchestrator`, and the `react-agent` /
  `codeact-agent` / `memact-agent` native loops. Setting
  `ABSTRACTGATEWAY_FLOWS_DIR` replaces that registry with a custom one.
- Agent sessions (every client: AbstractCode terminal + web, AbstractAssistant, your app):
  the gateway resolves `flow_id: "@default"` + `interface` to its
  `agents.default_workflow.<interface>` at every run start (built-in: shipped
  `basic-agent` for `abstractcode.agent.v1`; none for
  `abstractassistant.agent.v1`, whose app then runs its built-in orchestrator;
  an unresolvable default refuses the run, never falls back). Every run works in
  a folder on the gateway host (the conversation folder under
  `<data dir>/workspaces/`, or the terminal client's launch folder), browsable via
  `GET /runs/{id}/workspace[/files|/content]` (AbstractCode Files tab, `/files`),
  with a built-in deny list (credential folders, framework settings folders, the
  gateway data folder) for every run and the browser. The curated skill shelf
  ships in `abstractskill` and is seeded into `<data dir>/skills/registry` at each
  start (`skills.shelf` overrides). Live replies: `input_data._runtime.stream`,
  gateway default `agents.streaming_default`, `llm.delta` / `llm.delta_end`
  events on the run SSE stream (not ledger records); structured output, remote
  AbstractCore, entity chat do not stream. The console's **Open** starts the
  Assistant signed in through a one-time hand-over file. Public
  `GET /api/gateway/about` returns versions for About screens.
- Framework identity: `identity/abstractframework.json` is canonical; byte-identical
  copies live in abstractcore, the ui-kit, the AbstractCode terminal client and the
  gateway terminal console; `python3 scripts/check_identity_sync.py` verifies them and the
  shared contract fixtures (console, automations, gateway pointer).
- Browser apps are served by the gateway at `/apps/<app>/` (HTTP, SSE, WebSocket; one address
  and one tunnel for every app). App proxies (AbstractCode web server, Flow Editor server, ui-kit app-server) overwrite
  `X-Forwarded-For` with the browser's address and add `X-AbstractFramework-App-Proxy`;
  the gateway believes the header only from a loopback peer, so LAN browsers stay remote.
- Responsive: the gateway and AbstractCore web consoles and the five browser apps (Code web 0.8.0,
  Flow 0.5.0, Observer 0.4.0, Continuum 0.5.0, Entity 0.4.0, on `@abstractframework/ui-kit` 0.3.2)
  work on phones, tablets and any window size (breakpoints 480/768/1024/1440 px wide plus 500 px
  tall; drawers below 1024 px; bottom-sheet dialogs on phones; 44 px touch targets). A phone opens
  `/console` and `/apps/<app>/` on the gateway's address after `abstractgateway network set lan`.
- Email is per gateway user, set in the consoles, never with environment variables (the
  `ABSTRACT_EMAIL_*` variables were removed in 0.7.0; a leftover account is imported once). Two
  words: the user's **email address** (sign-in codes, "Forgot your token?", notifications, default
  allowed recipient; set in **Create user** or on the account page) and their **mailbox** (a
  connection: tabs **IMAP** (first, selected; address + password, server fields visible and
  pre-filled, no user name field) / **Google** / **Microsoft**; one **Connect**, then an **Active**
  switch, **Test** / **Disconnect**). Account page: web console **Accounts** (**Email** on your own
  row), `@` on the terminal console's Accounts screen,
  `PUT /api/gateway/me/email`. Notifications: two switches **Job failed** and
  **Approval needed** (on by default, sent only with a connected mailbox). **Agent email tools**: the
  user's switch, off by default, unavailable until a mailbox is connected. **Advanced**: recipient
  rules (a new account allows its own email address), send limits 100/h and 1000/day, watch folder.
  Administrators: under the accounts table, **Email for everyone** with one switch **Mailboxes for
  users** (on), and under Advanced **Agent email tools for users** (on) and **Sign-in by email** (on).
  The **Accounts** page is one table of users and entities (Create user / Create entity; per row
  Active switch, Email, Logs, Workspace, Rotate, Manage, Delete); an administrator sees every
  account, a user only themself and the entities they created. `email.received@1` automations read mail read-only, treat
  it as untrusted (links not followed; network, code and sending tools ask unless named in
  `policy.untrusted_input_tools`) and never run on the framework's own automatic mail
  (`Auto-Submitted`, `X-AbstractFramework-Automation`; `auto_submitted: "admit"` accepts others'
  automatic mail). Sign-in by email: one link, **Forgot your token? Email me a sign-in code**.

## Start Here

- [README.md](README.md): Ecosystem overview and install paths.
- [docs/README.md](docs/README.md): Docs index for this repo.
- [docs/install.md](docs/install.md): Mac installer (with the one-time Open Anyway step), one-line bootstrap (install.sh / install.ps1: what it does, options, CLI equivalents, run at login, Network setting, uninstall), upgrade (PyPI/crates.io index lag and network failures run the same full install again, then stop with exit 1 and the command to re-run; a port changed in a console is kept; anything left out, e.g. local voice on a system without its wheels, is said in red), terminal console and AbstractCode's terminal client built by default (`--no-console`, `--no-code-cli`), the commands you get (every command on PATH with what it does: `abstractgateway-config` is the gateway's admin command; all of AbstractCore's commands, its apps `summarizer`/`extractor`/`judge`/`intent`/`deepsearch` included, and the voice, vision and music commands, unless `--no-core-cli`; a package whose name is taken is left out), signing `abstractcode` in (`abstractcode login --token <admin token>` once, or `abstractgateway apps tui-command code` on the gateway's computer), headless or remote machine setup (the start-at-login question and the console offer over SSH, the terminal console with `--gateway-url` and `--token`, its Network screen `N`, one SSH tunnel for the console and every app at `/apps/<app>/`), the local gateway pointer, Light / Apple / GPU chooser, GPU on Linux and Windows (NVIDIA; measured install and per-capability timings on a Quadro RTX 5000; speech input set in the fresh setup and `av<19`, sequential CPU offload next to a loaded text model, loaded image models reused), right after a release (the index-lag and network retry), generated manifest contract.
- [docs/installers/README.md](docs/installers/README.md): Install design: script bootstrap + gateway console (strategy, per-OS journeys, components, OS security/sudo/UAC/execution policy, manifest, operations).
- [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md): Practical entry paths (core, runtime, gateway, UIs, bundles).
- [docs/agent-sessions.md](docs/agent-sessions.md): What every client shares when it chats with an agent: the gateway's default agent workflow (`agents.default_workflow.<interface>`), the conversation workspace on the gateway host and its built-in deny list, the curated skill shelf (`skills.shelf`), live replies (`agents.streaming_default` + per-client Stream replies; what does not stream), opening the Assistant signed in from the console.
- [AbstractGateway shipped workflows](https://github.com/lpalbou/AbstractGateway/blob/main/docs/shipped-workflows.md): Workflows a fresh Gateway install already serves (coder, deep research, co-scientist) + how to run one.
- [docs/automations.md](docs/automations.md): How automations work and how to manage them: an automation is a durable controller run, each tick an occurrence (a child run shown as a chat turn); independent vs configurable growing context (growing replays the most recent 50 000 tokens of whole turns); quiet by default (`notify` output, final failures, typed waits `ask_user` / `tool_approval` / `event`); creation is the tool consent (`policy.tool_approval` `auto`/`ask`, MCP tools still ask); creating from the Assistant (Schedule this conversation…), the Observer (Launch → Automate), AbstractCode (`/automations`, `/schedule`, the browser Automations section) or a workflow's `automation_defaults`; email automations (`email.received@1` with typed filters and hourly/60 s batches, each message once, untrusted input with network, code and sending tools asking unless named in `policy.untrusted_input_tools`, own automatic mail never an event, `auto_submitted: "admit"`; **Email result** = every completed result via `notify.channels` with `email` and `notify.recipients`, a switch in the form's **Mailbox** section; `policy.email_allowed_recipients`, only you by default); two worked examples with request bodies; pause / run now (also while paused) / resume without catch-up / revise / archive / discuss; restart safety; limits (fixed UTC intervals, triggers `schedule@1`, `email.received@1` and `manual@1`); troubleshooting. Needs a gateway advertising `contracts.common.automations` (AbstractGateway 0.6.0 and AbstractRuntime 0.6.0 and later; email automations need 0.8.0 of both).
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): How the stack fits together (Mermaid diagrams: components, distribution, how a turn flows, the live-reply lane, the framework identity flow), app proxies and the forwarded-address rule, model residency and eject.
- [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md): Minimal config, Core vs Gateway defaults, Network exposure, email accounts (per gateway user or per AbstractCore install; no environment variables; `--password-stdin`), client configuration.
- [docs/guide/email-integration.md](docs/guide/email-integration.md): Your email address and your own mailbox on the gateway: the account page, connecting a mailbox (IMAP / Google / Microsoft), recipient rules and send limits, agent email tools (off by default), email automations (new mail only, untrusted input, own automatic mail never triggers), notifications (Job failed, Approval needed), sign-in by email, the administrator's Mailboxes for users switch and the Accounts table, who sees which accounts, AbstractCore's own account.
- [docs/guide/deployment-iphone.md](docs/guide/deployment-iphone.md): Phones and tablets: the console and the browser apps on the gateway's one address (`/console`, `/apps/<app>/`), the Network setting, sign-in, what adapts on a small screen.
- [docs/api.md](docs/api.md): Meta-package API: release pins, helpers, `abstractframework doctor` and `manifest`.
- [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md): Common questions, comparisons, limits.
- [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md): Symptoms, checks and fixes (installer blocked by macOS, PyPI index lag right after a release, sign-in links and sign-in by email, ports, network access, providers, email automations and agent email tools, logs).
- [docs/glossary.md](docs/glossary.md): Shared terminology used across docs.
- [docs/workspace-scripts.md](docs/workspace-scripts.md): Working from source: package inventory (scripts/lib/packages.txt), dependency tiers, build/status/pull/commit/push scripts.
- [docs/adr/README.md](docs/adr/README.md): Cross-package ADR index and accepted platform contracts.

## Release Profile (Pinned Versions)

- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml): Single source of truth for pinned ecosystem versions and extras.
- [abstractframework/__init__.py](abstractframework/__init__.py): `RELEASE_VERSIONS`, `NPM_RELEASE_VERSIONS`, `CRATE_RELEASE_VERSIONS`, `get_release_profile()`, `print_status()`.
- [docs/installers/install-manifest.json](docs/installers/install-manifest.json): Generated install manifest, schema v2 (pins, profiles, npm apps, `bootstrap` gateway pin/scripts/flags, console-first `post_install`).
- [scripts/install.sh](scripts/install.sh) / [scripts/install.ps1](scripts/install.ps1): The bootstrap installers.
- abstractframework 0.10.0 pins (PyPI, `==`): abstractgateway 0.13.0, abstractassistant 0.13.0, abstractcore 2.25.0, AbstractRuntime 0.9.0, abstractagent 0.3.17, abstractskill 0.3.0, AbstractMemory 0.3.0, abstractsemantics 0.0.5, abstractvoice 0.14.0, abstractvision 0.3.33, abstractmusic 0.1.15, abstract3d 0.3.2.
- Released with it: npm `@abstractframework/flow` 0.8.0, `code` 0.11.0, `observer` 0.7.0, `continuum` 0.7.0, `entity` 0.7.0 (opened through the gateway at `/apps/<app>/`, or run with `npx`); crates (`CRATE_RELEASE_VERSIONS`) `abstractgateway-console` 0.15.0 (built by the installer by default), `abstractcore-console` 0.8.0, `abstractcode` 0.9.0, `abstracttui` 0.6.0; images `ghcr.io/lpalbou/abstractgateway:0.13.0`, `ghcr.io/lpalbou/abstractcore-server:2.25.0`.
- Profiles: light (remote-only), apple (`abstractframework[apple]`, macOS 14+ Apple Silicon), gpu (`abstractframework[gpu]`); Python 3.10-3.13 (F5-TTS voice cloning in apple/gpu needs 3.11+).

## Full Context

- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): Concatenated context for copy/paste into an LLM (`python scripts/gen_llms_full.py`; `--check` fails when it is stale).

## Optional

- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): Release history of the meta-package and its pins.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): Working on this repository (tests, doc regeneration, pull requests).
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): Reporting a vulnerability.
- [ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS.md](ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS.md): Credits.

- [AbstractCore](https://github.com/lpalbou/abstractcore): LLM providers, tools, structured output, media.
- [AbstractRuntime](https://github.com/lpalbou/abstractruntime): Durable execution (runs, effects, waits, ledger, stores).
- [AbstractAgent](https://github.com/lpalbou/abstractagent): Agent patterns (ReAct/CodeAct/MemAct) built on runtime + core.
- [AbstractFlow](https://github.com/lpalbou/abstractflow): npm web editor for VisualFlow authoring on top of AbstractGateway.
- [AbstractGateway](https://github.com/lpalbou/abstractgateway): HTTP/SSE control plane for gateway-first deployments.
- [AbstractCode](https://github.com/lpalbou/abstractcode): Terminal + web host UIs for durable runs.
